result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 2 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full existing application assessment, including unchanged source, scoped exclusively to eShopModernizedNTier. Reviewed 27 first-party source/config/project files plus Docker Compose configuration; source-to-sink inspection and whole-scope pattern searches, not a diff review.

Limitations: static source analysis only; application not executed, no exploit or load tests, runtime deployment/ACLs and platform internals not inspected. Generated code, obj/bin, .vs, temp and vendor artifacts excluded from CWE checklist source review. NOT_FOUND means no confirmed pattern in reviewed first-party code, not proof of absence. Specialist returned change-only results and was not used as full-workspace evidence.

All service mutations, instance/static state, startup and HiLo locking reviewed. Active service code has missing synchronization for shared database ID allocation. Commented-out singleton registrations and mock-only mutable lists do not establish active multithreaded singleton/shared-memory vulnerabilities. HiLo uses a private instance lock with automatic release; no incorrect lock acquisition/release or failed synchronization mechanism was confirmed. CWE-567 retained NOT_FOUND for shared in-memory/static data; database races are represented under CWE-662/CWE-820.

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: Confidence: high for non-atomic ID allocation; medium for deployed concurrent exploitability. CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem reads the shared database MAX(Id), increments it in process and later inserts. CreateAvailableStock similarly performs an existence check and MAX(StockId)+1 before SaveChanges. IDs explicitly use DatabaseGeneratedOption.None. Concurrent requests handled by separate WCF instances can both read the same maximum before either commits; the second insert then fails on the duplicate key, causing request/inventory-update failure. SaveChanges transactions do not encompass the earlier MAX read; there is no explicit encompassing serializable transaction or cross-request synchronization. WCF default per-session/per-call handling does not globally serialize separate clients. No stress test or deployment concurrency observation was performed. Database uniqueness may prevent corruption but does not prevent the failing request. CWE-662 and CWE-820 describe this same root cause, not independent exploits.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
